questions.questionText: What is JSX?
options: A syntax extension for JavaScript that lets you write HTML-like markup within a JavaScript file
questions.correctAnswer: A syntax extension for JavaScript that lets you write HTML-like markup within a JavaScript file
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) A syntax extension for JavaScript that lets you write HTML-like markup within a JavaScript file.

questions.questionText: Which statement about browsers and JSX is correct?
options: Browsers require JSX only for CSS
Browsers do not understand JSX, so it is converted into JavaScript
questions.correctAnswer: Browsers do not understand JSX, so it is converted into JavaScript
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Browsers do not understand JSX, so it is converted into JavaScript.

questions.questionText: Which tools convert JSX into JavaScript that the browser can understand?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Webpack and Babel.

questions.questionText: In the early days of Web development, how were content, design, and logic kept?
options: Content in HTML, design in CSS, and logic in JavaScript, usually in separate files
questions.correctAnswer: Content in HTML, design in CSS, and logic in JavaScript, usually in separate files
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Content in HTML, design in CSS, and logic in JavaScript, usually in separate files.

questions.questionText: In ReactJS, where do rendering logic and markup live?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) In the same place - components.

questions.questionText: What is the benefit of keeping a button's rendering logic and markup together?
options: They stay in sync with each other on every edit
They are stored on the server
questions.correctAnswer: They stay in sync with each other on every edit
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) They stay in sync with each other on every edit.

questions.questionText: Why is it safe to change the code of unrelated components, such as the sidebar and a button, independently?
options: Because components share the same variables
Because each component's markup is isolated from the others
questions.correctAnswer: Because each component's markup is isolated from the others
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Because each component's markup is isolated from the others.

questions.questionText: JSX looks much like HTML but is:
options: A bit stricter and can display dynamic information
Less strict and cannot display dynamic information
questions.correctAnswer: A bit stricter and can display dynamic information
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) A bit stricter and can display dynamic information.

questions.questionText: How many rules must JSX follow, as discussed in the session?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Three.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the three JSX rules?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Always use lowercase component names.

questions.questionText: Which rule applies to returning multiple elements from a component?
options: Multiple elements can be returned directly without any wrapper
Only two elements can be returned
Multiple elements must be wrapped within a single parent tag
Multiple elements must be separated by commas
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple elements must be wrapped within a single parent tag
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Multiple elements must be wrapped within a single parent tag.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be used to wrap multiple JSX elements without adding an extra DOM node?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) <></> (Fragment).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a valid wrapper for multiple elements in JSX?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer is C) Both
and <>.

questions.questionText: In JSX, a self-closing tag such as must be written as:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) <img/>.

questions.questionText: In JSX, <li>Badminton must be written as:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer is A)
  • Badminton
    • .

questions.questionText: Why does Code Snippet 4 (copied HTML with unclosed <li> tags and multiple root elements) not work in JSX?
options: Because JSX does not support lists
Because lists are not allowed in React
Because JSX is stricter than HTML and has rules that must be followed
questions.correctAnswer: Because JSX is stricter than HTML and has rules that must be followed
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Because JSX is stricter than HTML and has rules that must be followed.

questions.questionText: In JSX, the HTML class attribute is written as:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) className.

questions.questionText: Why can the word "class" not be used as an attribute name in JSX?
options: It is used only in Redux
It is a reserved word in JavaScript
questions.correctAnswer: It is a reserved word in JavaScript
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) It is a reserved word in JavaScript.

questions.questionText: Which SVG attribute is correctly written in JSX?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) strokeWidth.

questions.questionText: Which of the following attributes keeps its dashes in JSX?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) aria-* and data-*.

questions.questionText: Why are attributes written in camelCase in JSX?
options: Because JSX turns into JavaScript and attributes become keys of JavaScript objects, which have naming limitations
questions.correctAnswer: Because JSX turns into JavaScript and attributes become keys of JavaScript objects, which have naming limitations
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Because JSX turns into JavaScript and attributes become keys of JavaScript objects, which have naming limitations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct JSX attribute for the CSS class "user-name"?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) className="user-name".

questions.questionText: Which symbols open a window to JavaScript inside JSX markup?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) { }.

questions.questionText: Curly braces {} in JSX are also known as:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Template syntax.

questions.questionText: In const name = "Mark"; {name}, what is displayed?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Mark.

questions.questionText: How should a string attribute be passed to JSX?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Within single or double quotes.

questions.questionText: If an attribute like src needs a value taken dynamically from a JavaScript variable, how is it written?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) src={pic}.

questions.questionText: What is the output of where pic and name are JavaScript variables?
options: It uses the variable values for src and alt
It prints the words pic and name
questions.correctAnswer: It uses the variable values for src and alt
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) It uses the variable values for src and alt.

questions.questionText: Which JavaScript array method is used to transform an array of strings into an array of components?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) map().

questions.questionText: Why is map() used in JSX to display a list of components?
options: It converts an array of data into an array of JSX elements
questions.correctAnswer: It converts an array of data into an array of JSX elements
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) It converts an array of data into an array of JSX elements.

questions.questionText: In {names.map((nm) => <Welcome name={nm} />)}, what is nm?
options: The current item of the array passed as a prop to Welcome
questions.correctAnswer: The current item of the array passed as a prop to Welcome
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) The current item of the array passed as a prop to Welcome.

questions.questionText: In {names.map(...)}, why are the outer curly braces required?
options: To evaluate the JavaScript expression inside JSX
questions.correctAnswer: To evaluate the JavaScript expression inside JSX
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) To evaluate the JavaScript expression inside JSX.

questions.questionText: Which statement about {users.map((usr) => <User name={usr.name} pic={usr.pic} />)} is correct?
options: It converts an array of objects into an array of User components
It creates a single User component
questions.correctAnswer: It converts an array of objects into an array of User components
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) It converts an array of objects into an array of User components.

questions.questionText: Which JSX code correctly defines a component taking name and pic as destructured props?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) function User({ name, pic }) { ... }.

questions.questionText: Which file is used in the session to hold the CSS code for the examples?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) App.css.

questions.questionText: Which CSS property is used to make an image a perfect circle together with equal height and width?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) border-radius: 50%.

questions.questionText: Which CSS property is used so that an image is zoomed in and not stretched?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) object-fit: cover.

questions.questionText: Which CSS property keeps height and width the same for an image?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) aspect-ratio: 1/1.

questions.questionText: HTML is described as a "forgiving language" because:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Closing <li> tags are optional.

questions.questionText: In the session, which component takes name and pic as props so both values can be displayed?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) User.

questions.questionText: What does the summary say about JSX?
options: It separates logic and view into different files
It is used to keep related logic and view in one place
questions.correctAnswer: It is used to keep related logic and view in one place
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) It is used to keep related logic and view in one place.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the correct return of multiple elements in a component?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer is C) return (
...
);.

questions.questionText: Which of the following causes an error in JSX?
options: Returning multiple elements without a wrapper
questions.correctAnswer: Returning multiple elements without a wrapper
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Returning multiple elements without a wrapper.

questions.questionText: JSX can return multiple elements without any wrapper. This statement is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) False.

questions.questionText: Template syntax supports expressions. This statement is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) True.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct JSX way to render an <h2> that includes a styled span containing a name variable?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer is B)

Hello, {name}

.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes nesting JSX elements as used in this session?
options: Using map() to produce multiple components from a collection of data
questions.correctAnswer: Using map() to produce multiple components from a collection of data
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Using map() to produce multiple components from a collection of data.
